summary: Ohio State’s trip to Texas puts protection and quarterback containment under a sharper test. Watch the starting line, the edge rotation and who gets open if Texas sends extra attention toward the primary receiver.

items.headline: Russaw cleared for Texas, according to On3
items.tldr: His Ohio State debut is expected Saturday. Watch how the edge rotation changes and whether fresh legs help the pass rush finish without opening an escape lane.

items.headline: Day keeps the starting offensive line under evaluation
items.tldr: Watch the right side’s communication and the opening combination. Treat practice rotation as preparation; it does not by itself establish a change in starters.

items.headline: Every McCuin catch in the opener moved the chains or scored
items.tldr: If Texas rolls help toward Smith, watch whether McCuin can keep the next option productive. A routine conversion may be more revealing than a contested deep ball.

items.headline: Ball State’s quarterback escaped Ohio State’s pressure
items.tldr: Against Manning, watch where the pass rush leaves space. Making him move is only useful if the defense can finish the play before he finds a running lane.

items.headline: Traveling to Austin? DKR’s map locates gates and water
items.tldr: Choose your entrance before arriving and save the map on your phone. The web version also marks first aid and restrooms.

lead.headline: Protect the pocket. Close the escape.
lead.body: Watch whether the offensive line can work as one and the pass rush can finish under control. Both jobs get harder when one player leaves a gap.

matchup.question: What should Ohio State prove at Texas?
matchup.answer: Keep protection connected on offense. On defense, force the quarterback to move without leaving a clean lane out of the pocket.

signals.title: Protection
signals.detail: Watch the opening combination and how it handles defensive movement. Changing a blocker is only useful if the whole line stays connected.

signals.title: Containment
signals.detail: Watch the outside defender when Manning steps up or rolls away. Pressure needs a second defender in position to finish.

signals.title: Receiver balance
signals.detail: If Texas tilts help toward Smith, watch the next target. Sustaining a drive may depend on the receiver working away from that attention.
